edge_cases.scenario: A small-business owner is contacted by the in-house collections department of the bank that originally extended a commercial line of credit; the department uses the name 'Asset Recovery Group' and never gives a mini-Miranda disclosure.
edge_cases.gap_description: Neither the logic nor the checklist requires any threshold facts about whether the entity is a 'debt collector' under §1692a(6) (original creditors collecting their own debts in their own name are generally excluded) or whether the obligation is a consumer debt for personal, family, or household purposes under §1692a(5). Applied as encoded, the node would find independent (11) and (14) violations for a commercial debt collected by an exempt original creditor, telling the user they have an FDCPA claim when the statute does not apply at all.

edge_cases.scenario: A collection law firm files a summons and complaint in state court to collect a credit card debt; the pleadings themselves contain no statement that the communication is from a debt collector, and the consumer asks whether that is a §1692e(11) violation.
edge_cases.gap_description: §1692e(11) expressly exempts 'a formal pleading made in connection with a legal action,' and Reg F §1006.18(e)(3) carries the exception forward. The checklist's dispositive item ('whether the collector disclosed in EACH subsequent communication that it was a debt collector') contains no pleading carve-out, so the node would report a violation where none exists — a common scenario since most consumers encountering collectors in litigation receive pleadings without mini-Miranda language.
